sections.overview: Platalina genovensium is a nectar-feeding bat found on the arid western slopes of the Andes, from Peru to northern Chile.
sections.identification: Its elongated muzzle is distinctive; its body is about 8 cm long and the forearm measures roughly 5 cm.
sections.habitat: It forages in dry areas with columnar cacti and uses cracks, abandoned mine shafts and tunnels as roosts.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on cactus nectar and pollen, while also eating fruit and insects; Haageocereus pollen was especially frequent in a study at Lachay.
sections.behavior: Field captures in southwestern Peru show that it is active after dusk.
sections.reproduction: Pregnant and lactating females have been recorded in March in Peru, but reproduction remains poorly documented.
sections.ecology: Pollen carried on its fur suggests that it pollinates some cacti and bromeliads in the lomas ecosystem.
sections.conservation: A 2020 species review reported a global IUCN category of Near Threatened; it identifies habitat loss and dependence on columnar cacti as concerns.
